title: Make Project and Worktree operations truthful
why: Project and Worktree controls cross the web client, typed contracts, daemon inventory, Git, persisted identity, and Codex checkout hooks. Several seams could report or display state that did not match what Git or the daemon had actually done: existing-branch intent was dropped, origin-less repositories could collide, transient discovery failures pruned stable identity, dirty deletion forced data loss, and loading or open failures could appear blank.
how:
Carry explicit existing and force intent through contracts into daemon-owned Git operations; preflight dirty worktrees, preserve truthful partial outcomes after destructive effects, and roll back failed creation. Keep origin-less identity tied to the exact common Git directory and distinguish missing repositories from temporarily unavailable discovery. Derive eligible existing branches from authoritative inventory, centralize selection after successful open, and show loading, error, offline, and non-Git workspace states. Remove the retired project-level setup override so trusted Actions remain the lifecycle owner. Make Codex bootstrap hooks fall back to the harness checkout and protect that contract with a disposable detached-worktree regression. Validation covers 3,562 tests, all builds and script tests, plus the live browser and isolated Electron client.

Keep the structured semantic document and tracked storage manifest in separate files. New promotions write manifest.json while canvas.json remains the semantic v2 entry; readers retain read-only fallback for legacy HTML and Markdown bundles whose manifest is canvas.json. Reserve manifest.json so a generic entry or asset cannot be overwritten at promotion.
